en.title: Build a Revision Plan
en.description: Create a structured revision plan from lecture notes using AI.
en.outcome: You can use AI to create effective, personalized revision plans from your study materials.
en.explanation: AI can help organize your study materials into a revision plan, but you need to guide it with your priorities, available time, and learning style.

worked_example.scenario: Preparing for Database Systems exam from lecture notes.
worked_example.bad_attempt: Help me study for my exam.
worked_example.good_attempt:
Goal: Create a 5-day revision plan for my Database Systems exam.
Context: Topics covered: ER diagrams, normalization (1NF-3NF), SQL queries, transactions, indexing. Exam in 6 days.
Constraints: 2 hours/day. Start with weakest topics (normalization, transactions). Include practice questions for each topic.
Output: Day-by-day schedule with specific topics, time allocation, and practice activities.
worked_example.why_better: Specifies topics, time constraints, priorities, and desired format.

interactive_task.instruction:
Create a revision plan using these lecture notes excerpt:

"CS201 - Database Systems
Week 1-3: ER diagrams, relational model
Week 4-6: Normalization (1NF, 2NF, 3NF, BCNF)
Week 7-9: SQL (SELECT, JOIN, subqueries, aggregations)
Week 10-11: Transactions, ACID properties, concurrency
Week 12: Indexing, B-trees, query optimization

Exam: 40% theory, 60% practical (SQL + design)"
hints: How many days do you have? How many hours per day?
Which topics need more time based on the exam format?
Include practice activities, not just reading.
interactive_task.sample_good_response:
Goal: Create a 7-day revision plan for CS201 Database Systems exam.
Context: Exam is 40% theory, 60% practical. Topics span ER diagrams through query optimization.
Constraints: 2-3 hours/day. Allocate more time to SQL and normalization (high exam weight). Include at least 2 practice problems per topic. Mix theory review with hands-on SQL practice.
Output: Day-by-day table with: Topic | Time | Activity (read/practice/review) | Practice Questions.
evaluation_criteria: Includes a clear study goal with timeline
Prioritizes topics based on exam format
Specifies time constraints
Includes practice activities

understanding_checks.question: Why should a revision plan prioritize certain topics?
options: Some topics carry more exam weight and need more time
All topics should get equal time regardless
AI decides what's important
Prioritizing means skipping topics
understanding_checks.explanation: If the exam is 60% practical, SQL and design deserve more revision time than purely theoretical topics.

understanding_checks.question: What makes a revision plan better than just 'studying everything'?
options: Structure, time management, and targeted practice
It's longer and more detailed
It eliminates the need to study
It guarantees good grades
understanding_checks.explanation: A structured plan helps you allocate time effectively, identify weak areas, and include active practice.

feedback_templates.pass: Excellent plan! Your instruction balances theory and practice.
feedback_templates.partial: Good start. Consider adding specific practice activities for each day.
feedback_templates.fail: Try again. Think about: how many days, hours per day, and which topics need more time.

en.retry_hint: Review the worked example and try again.
en.recap: You practiced creating study plans with AI. Key: specify time constraints, priorities, and include active practice, not just reading.

glossary_terms.definition: A structured schedule for reviewing study material before an exam.
